definition: Reputable means having a good, trustworthy reputation; respectable and legitimate.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reputable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reputable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Before hiring movers, Dad called three references to make sure the company was actually reputable.
Acceptable means merely good enough; reputable means the good name has been checked and holds up — people vouch for it.
Distinguished goes beyond reputable: not just trustworthy, but standing out above its trustworthy peers.

Trustworthy means deserving of confidence: this person or source will not cheat you or let you down. Reputable adds the public track record — not just trustworthy in fact but known to be, with reviews and references others can check. Trustworthiness lives in conduct; a reputation can be looked up.

Respectable means meeting society's standards — proper, presentable, nothing anyone would raise an eyebrow at. Reputable is more practical: it says a business or source has a verified record of honest dealing. A shop can look perfectly respectable and still cheat you; reputable is about the record, not appearances.

The first seller had no reviews, a blurry photo, and wanted payment by gift card.
The second had eight years on the platform, four hundred detailed reviews, a return policy, and answered Kira's questions within the hour.
"Same guitar, but only one reputable seller," her brother said.
"Pay the one with the track record."
The years of history, hundreds of reviews, clear policies, and prompt answers form the trustworthy track record that makes the second seller reputable — and the first one not.

After the hailstorm, roofing crews Amber had never heard of went door to door offering same-day repairs at half price.
Her grandfather waved them off.

'They collect deposits, patch a few shingles, and vanish before the first leak.' Instead he spent the evening doing what he called his homework: reading five years of customer reviews, calling two neighbors the company listed as references, and checking its license with the state board.
'Anyone can promise good work,' he told Amber.

'A reputable company is one whose promises other people have already tested — the record is public, and it holds up.' The crew he finally hired cost more and came later, but the roof outlasted the next three storms, exactly as its record said it would.
